Industry News: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1466 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences.
  • The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information.
  • It has been revealed that published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.

The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.

It has been revealed that published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.

"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," noted Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab.".

How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes.

In a recent development, for decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.

It has been revealed that visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.

The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.

Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back.".

It has been revealed that the new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.

Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man.

Recent findings suggest that an notable opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.

According to recent reports, at Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.

Recent findings suggest that when researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.

In a recent development, producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.

To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.

Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.

AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise.

Recent findings suggest that when the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The fresh approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.

Another notable discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.

In a recent development, this distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.

"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation.".

It has been revealed that the findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.

Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person.

According to recent reports, A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.

This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.

It has been revealed that the participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.

Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.

Sources indicate that the AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.

By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.

"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler mentioned. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around.".

A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight.

According to recent reports, the research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration.".

The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.

Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.

Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

Latest Update: The Pros And Cons Of Importing A Japanese Mini Truck

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that japan's tiny kei trucks have become a massive novelty in the U.S.
  • Sources indicate that the most glaring pro here is the low entry price.
  • Recent findings suggest that models such as the Honda Acty, Suzuki Carry, Daihatsu Hijet, Subaru Sambar, and Mitsubishi Minicab all have decades of production behind them, along with a knack for toughness and reliability.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that japan's tiny kei trucks have become a massive novelty in the U.S. — even for road-tripping — with 7,500 imported in 2023 alone. Whether bringing one home makes sense, though, depends on what you want to do with it.

Sources indicate that the most glaring pro here is the low entry price. Since they have to be 25 years old or older to be imported, it's perhaps unsurprising that — depending on condition — these used mini trucks generally sell for $4,500 to $10,000, before shipping and registration fees . The price lets enthusiasts from any tax bracket enjoy the amenities of the simple, durable — and, importantly, mechanically uncomplicated — trucks.

Recent findings suggest that models such as the Honda Acty, Suzuki Carry, Daihatsu Hijet, Subaru Sambar, and Mitsubishi Minicab all have decades of production behind them, along with a knack for toughness and reliability. And their small footprint makes them handy for farms, trade jobs, and urban delivery runs that would frustrate a full-size pickup, while also offering low fuel consumption.

In a recent development, but despite the benefits of these kei trucks on paper, know that legal and regulatory adversities can vary from state to state. There also can be unforeseen costs and safety concerns that present a real challenge for prospective buyers.

According to recent reports, the notorious 25-year federal law applies to kei trucks, counted from the month of manufacture rather than the model year. Being mindful of build dates before you buy can help avoid any holdups. Even when your mini truck clears customs, though, that doesn't guarantee license plates.

California is the hardest case, with most kei trucks that satisfy the federal age rule still unable to be registered because they don't meet emissions and safety regulations. Elsewhere the rules vary — states like Wyoming and Arkansas bar use on interstate highways while others like Georgia refuse road registration outright. Concern over how these trucks fare in a collision has led several states to crack down.

Shipping costs, customs and registration all add a few more thousand dollars on top of the sticker price — finding a reputable importer takes legwork, and the wait for shipping and customs clearance can last months. Once you've navigated that, insurance can pose another hurdle as some agents and systems may not be able to accommodate kei trucks. And though these tiny trucks are touted for their robust builds, sustained stateside highway speeds wear down parts faster and finding replacements is hard, as those parts aren't stocked at ordinary auto parts stores.

For a farm, estate, or enthusiast collection in a state with friendly rules, a kei truck can be a rewarding purchase, so long as you confirm your state's registration rules first. If all you need is a cheap light-duty pickup, however, several other examples are readily available. Perhaps a Ford Maverick might just be what you need.

Tech Report: Wiz ties Microsoft Agent Framework package compromise to release pipeline certificate

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (946 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.
  • It has been revealed that the malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine upgrade to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month.
  • Researchers at cloud security manufacturer Wiz Inc.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:44 EST / NOVEMBER 19 2026.

Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.

It has been revealed that the malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine upgrade to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month. Both versions were pulled from PyPI within about an hour, but anyone who installed them in that window is at risk.

Researchers at cloud security manufacturer Wiz Inc. have since found that the attacker appears to have gained publishing access using a client certificate and private key for Microsoft’s Engineering System Release Pipeline, an internal service the company uses to sign and publish packages. Address filtering on the service blocked the attacker’s first attempt from Amazon Web Services, according to Wiz, though the attacker was able to publish on a second try from Microsoft-owned address space.

Industry observers note that how the attacker obtained the credentials is not known. Microsoft had not responded to a request for comment from BleepingComputer as of Wednesday.

Industry observers note that the researchers also observed part of the operation, as the attacker’s tooling was reporting its progress to the same public webhook it was using to collect stolen data. The tooling identified itself as Cairn, an open-source penetration-testing framework that uses AI.

The malware itself is delivered through a .pth file added to both releases, a type of file Python runs every time it starts, meaning the credential stealer runs even if the framework itself is never imported. The two versions also kept the genuine agent-framework-core 1.26.0 as a dependency, so the framework continued to work normally while the malware ran in the background.

Industry observers note that once running, the malware collects secrets from environment variables and from other running processes, along with credential files for services such as Azure, npm, Git, Docker and Hugging Face. It also requests Azure managed identity tokens for 12 resources, according to application security tech giant Endor Labs Inc., with the second version adding requests for GitHub Actions tokens. The stolen data is then compressed, encoded and sent to a webhook.site address controlled by the attacker.

Researchers at malware tracking site OpenSourceMalware described the malware as a “focused credential and token stealer, not a remote access trojan,” noting that it does not install any persistence on infected systems.

Recent findings suggest that wiz’s analysis suggests the number of victims may be small, though it covers only the 50 requests the attacker’s free webhook.site account retained. Of those, 17 represented only three unique successful thefts of victim data, with the rest coming from the attacker’s own machines and from sandbox and security vendor scanning.

The incident is not the first this year involving an official Microsoft Python package. In May, Microsoft’s durabletask package was hijacked after its PyPI token was stolen in an attack that has been linked to TeamPCP, the group also behind the compromise of LiteLLM. Wiz notes it has not linked the two incidents.

Anyone who installed either of the malicious versions is being urged to treat it as a credential compromise, according to researchers, who recommend rebuilding from version 1.26.0 and rotating any secrets the affected systems could access.

“A list of dependencies in production might show no trace of the framework, while a build runner could have installed it and been shut down before the alert arrived,” James Matchett, head of security at software supply chain security organization Cloudsmith Ltd., told SiliconANGLE.

“If that runner had access to a deployment token, the team needs to know which version it installed and what the token could access,” he added.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The investment is structured as a combination of equity and growth financing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes
Longevity platform Hone Health nabs $228M to build out offerings" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Hone Health, a physician-led virtual longevity care platform, has raised $228 million.

The investment is structured as a combination of equity and growth financing. The $28 million series A extension was led by MarcyPen Capital Partners, with participation from Pentland Ventures, Kinship Ventures, Hanwha, Gannet Capital, humbition and Comma Capital. Other angel investors also participated, including the Jonas brothers. The $200 million in growth financing came from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

Hone will use the investment to support a number of expansions. It aims to launch more programming for metabolic health, PMOS, inflammation and immunity, and to launch a physician-supervised peptide program. It will add more diagnostics, including coronary CT angiography and gut microbiome analysis.

Industry observers note that hone also aims to continue building out its AI operating system that brings data together to help personalize care. And it plans to build out clinical trial infrastructure to support pharma partners.

In a recent development, “Longevity is thought of as this super exotic thing. […] I actually think longevity is now becoming primary care,” Saad Alam, co-founder and CEO of Hone, told Fierce Healthcare.

It costs $65 to test for 70 biomarkers with Hone, followed by a clinician consult with the option to add more diagnostics. Labs, health history, symptoms and medications are run through its AI, which then gives providers treatment recommendations. Hone can keep adding additional diagnostics and medications, per Alam, “and the AI gets smarter as we get more patients into that system.”.

Sources indicate that additionally, Hone is publicly announcing Hone Black, a new concierge longevity membership that has operated in stealth for a select group of patients for the past year. It combines diagnostics on over 1,600 health markers with ongoing medical care from physicians. Offerings include prescriptions, supplements, peptides and lifestyle guidance, plus exosome and stem cell therapies.

Recent findings suggest that alam founded the company after experiencing a shift in his health at 35 years old, including mental health issues, depression and weight gain. His doctor was initially of little help. It took Alam a year to find out he had low testosterone, and after treatment, he finally felt back on track. That experience, along with his father dying from kidney disease and his mother going through early menopause, opened his eyes to the longevity space.

It has been revealed that “This whole concept of longevity is going to be one of the single greatest problems I can dedicate my life to solving,” Alam realized at the time. He experimented with everything, from peptides to cold plunges to meditation.

Hone is a subsidiary of Time Therapeutics, which aims to support production of drugs that help people live longer. Alam, who started his career doing market research at Eli Lilly, knew clinical trials are expensive and inaccessible. He wanted to create a organization that could help commercialize drugs. The first step to that is Hone, or a DTC virtual care company that can capture longitudinal data on patients. The next phase will be publishing research. Finally, Hone will look to partner with pharma to get drugs to market faster.

The manufacturer has been providing care for five years, treating about 200,000 patients to date. It requires patients to have a physician and get bloodwork every 90 days in order to get medication refills. Members can contact their clinician between sessions as needed.

“We make sure, for the most part, that you are doing bloodwork and talking to a physician, a real conversation with a physician, in order to get prescribed medication,” Alam remarked.

Recent findings suggest that it isn’t about overprescribing medications. It’s about finding the most personalized protocol for each patient. “The companies that have—no pun intended—longevity are the ones that are going to figure out how to reduce the number of medications somebody might need,” Alam said.

It has been revealed that hone began with hormone therapy, then moved into longevity care with biomarker analysis and women’s health. Two months ago, Hone’s offerings for women surpassed offerings for men in terms of net fresh members. It soon prepares to run clinical trials on poly-chronic patients as well to help determine the right drug at the right time. Hone crossed $100 million in revenue in 2025, per Alam, and is on track to double this year.

Sources indicate that “When I started goop, wellness was a niche conversation,” Gwyneth Paltrow, founder and CEO of goop and co-founder of Kinship Ventures, mentioned in a press release. “Today, it’s one of the biggest categories in the world, and the next step is bringing real health and wellness to the masses, not just the few. Saad has built Hone to do exactly that, with serious science and at real scale. That’s why Kinship invested, and we could not be more excited about what’s ahead.”.

Hone will soon offer 14 longevity care categories, which Alam argues is akin to primary care. He estimates that Hone only refers to in-person care about 10% of the time, usually for higher-acuity conditions. Some Hone patients are already healthy; most are sick and willing to pay out of pocket because the current system has been inadequate in solving their health needs, per Alam.

In a recent development, “This is just the beginning of not only a way but a complete change in the way that medicine is practiced,” Alam said. “A lot of other companies are what I’ll call pill mills, and where we’ve really focused—our energy is making sure that we go through the more difficult work of managing the long-term health of our patients.”.

EV Share Jumps to 68%(!) and Small BEVs Rise to Power — China EV Sales Report for October

💡 Key Takeaways
  • High gas prices and a never-ending wave of new BEVs have allowed October to reach 68% EV market share, a new record!
  • According to recent reports, this record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash.
  • Industry observers note that adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (23% share) meant that in October a record 68% of all cars sold in China had a plug!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High gas prices and a never-ending wave of new BEVs have allowed October to reach 68% EV market share, a new record!

According to recent reports, this record achievement is thanks to a significant ICE (internal combustion engine) crash. The overall market dropped 27% year over year (YoY), to around 1.6 million sales. Plugins were down 14% YoY, but pure ICE sales were much worse off, crashing 44% YoY!

Industry observers note that adding 45% BEV share to PHEVs (23% share) meant that in October a record 68% of all cars sold in China had a plug! If this trend continues in the future, the Chinese market will be fully electrified by 2030, and will be 100% BEV before 2035!

This great result pulled the 2026 share up, to 59%, already 5% above the full year result of 2025. BEVs on their own were up to 40% (versus 33% in 2025).

At this pace, I expect the final number for 2026 EV share in China to be above 60%, with BEVs alone north of the 40% mark. And when the largest global automotive market gets this electrified … then the ICE industry is in serious trouble.

The ICE extinction is also visible in the overall ranking. The overall top 10 was fully made by EVs. Again.

Looking at the best sellers in several size categories, the ICE extinction is also quite visible. Although, once again, the C-segment/compact category is the exception, with the only ICE representative showing up there — the Toyota RAV4, in 2nd, behind the leader Nevo Q05 and just ahead of the BYD Dolphin.

Having a quick look at the five size categories, the highlight is the B-segment/subcompact category, which is the hottest segment right now, with three of the top four top sellers in October belonging to this category.

Considering that 56% of the newly introduced SUVs launched this year were bigger than 5 meters/197 inches, there is a clear disconnect between what people want (small hatchbacks/crossovers) and what OEMs offer (large SUVs).

Another highlight is the fact that Xiaomi had a gold plus silver win in the full size category, with the BYD Great Tang closing out the podium while the midsize category podium was 100% BYD Group.

Here’s more info and commentary on October’s top selling electric models:.

Recent findings suggest that A BYD Dolphin for BYD Seagull money ($10,000). This was Geely’s internal memo to describe the formula for the Geely Xingyuan when developing its star model. With an interesting name — Xingyuan translates as “wishing upon a star” — it seems that Geely had its wish granted. However, the Geely model will have a tough adversary soon, as the upcoming generation Seagull will land with only one goal — to steal the Xingyuan’s best seller status. But while the new Seagull didn’t land, the small Geely scored a record performance in October, with its 50,190 registrations representing a 14% increase YoY. Besides the new BYD Seagull, Geely’s hatchback now has to deal with Leapmotor’s B-segment contenders, the A10 and A05; the new-generation Wuling Bingo; Chery’s new QQ3; and let’s not forget about BYD’s Yuan Up, too.

BYD’s midsize SUV continues to transition into the fresh generation. Thanks to the ramp-up of the new Ultra body, BYD’s star player was 2nd, scoring 30,772 registrations. Sales were up by 6% compared to the same month last year. The new Ultra generation features lidar and 1,500 kW DC charging, and these two features aren’t even the most impressive aspects of the model! That would be the price. It starts at 152,000 yuan (or $22,000) with the 76 kWh battery, and it goes up to 180,000 yuan (or $26,000) with the 83 kWh battery. For comparison, the Tesla Model Y starts in China at 259,000 yuan ($38,250)…. Expect the Song to experience a second youth from here onwards, and while it is impossible to displace the Tesla Model Y from the runner-up spot, the last place on the podium is doable this year. And maybe higher up in 2027?

According to recent reports, BYD’s small crossover continues to surprise, thanks to recently improved specs. BYD’s team player rose to 3rd in October, scoring 28,514 registrations, which was a 44% increase YoY and a fresh record score. Despite not being the most exciting vehicle to look at, or drive, the truth is that it is surfing the wave of small, affordable EVs better than most, scoring high in value for money with prices starting at $11,000 and higher end versions having BYD’s driver-assistance system. With small vehicles currently having a moment in China, expect the small crossover to show up in the top 5 more regularly.

Recent findings suggest that things continue to go well for the startup brand, with its newly introduced baby A10 now established as the star player in an already strong lineup. Thanks to 27,247 registrations, the small crossover managed another top 5 presence. The model has the usual value-for-money focus of the brand, and a low, low price of 66,000 yuan ($10,000). On top of that, however, the A10 offers something close to a distinct personality, as the design eschews the white product standard design of Leapmotor for something more personal, mostly thanks to the front and back lights and a floating roof effect. With B-segment BEVs now being the hottest category in China, Leapmotor is well prepared to benefit from the subcompact rising tide, thanks to the recent arrival of the A10 small crossover and its sibling, the A05 small hatchback. Talk about perfect timing….

After the SU7 and YU7, Xiaomi has another success on its hands. This significant fat SUV — or shall I say SUVs, as the lineup is broken down between the 7-seat N90 and the 5-seat N70 — scored 27,132 registrations in only its second month on the market, pulling it immediately into the overall top 5. Even with the number of competitors growing every passing day, Xiaomi’s upcoming land yachts have been selling like hot cakes, while drying up sales of the competition. Proof of that, is the fact that there were only two full size models in October’s top 20, with the other being … the Xiaomi SU7.

Looking at the rest of the best seller table, there were a number of models hitting record scores, starting with the #8 Nevo Q05 (20,022 units) continuing its success story. The #10 Bestune Xiaoma (17,887 units) benefitted from a recent refresh to score a surprise record score. Could this mean that small city EVs are (finally) seeing the light at the end of the tunnel?

As for the second half of the table, the highlight is the ramp-up of the Xpeng L03, with the attractive looking crossover, which kind of reminds of a mini-Lotus or small Polestar, reaching 13th thanks to 15,653 sales. This EV looks to be the startup’s star model thanks to a competitive price (124,000 RMB) that is half the price of the Tesla Model Y!

Other models with record performances were the #14 MG 4 (15,503 units), with the fresh generation proving to be much more popular and adaptable to local tastes than the previous one, and the #17 Chery QQ3 EV, which continued its slow climb in the ranking thanks to 14,041 sales, which made it the 5th B-segment model in the top 20.

Still in the top 20, we should also highlight the best selling foreign model, the Tesla Model Y VW ID.Aura T6, the new China-made (and China-developed) German crossover that has allowed Volkswagen to beat the Texans for the first time in years (the Tesla Model Y was down 60% YoY, to 7,807 units, while the Model 3 was down 85%, to 1,010 units). The Aura T6, VW’s take on the Model Y formula, rose to the 20th position in its first full month on the market!

Sources indicate that A promising sign, or just hype? Only time will tell, but at least for now, VW seems to be getting some traction on the EV side of the Chinese market, a point also highlighted by the fact that it wasn’t just the Aura T6 getting decent sales. The also newly introduced VW ID.Era 5S (think Chinese VW Jetta) got 7,100 registrations in October. Is there hope after all?

It has been revealed that outside the top 20, the main event was the ramp-up of Nevo’s new baby, the Q06, which is looking to replicate the Q05’s success in the category above. With some 10,000 registrations in only its second month, it looks like it could join the top 20 soon. The same can be remarked about the Geely Galaxy TT, the make’s answer to the Xiaomi SU7, which had around 10,500 deliveries in October. Then there’s also the BYD Yuan Plus, which, after a long cross through the desert, seems to be picking up steam again. It scored 11,658 registrations last month, a new year best.

Looking at the 2026 ranking, the podium remained the same, and unless something unexpected happens, it should stay as it is until the end of the year, with the small Geely repeating its 2025 win. That also means the Tesla Model Y will return to silver after getting bronze in 2025, and the BYD Song will get back onto the podium after a one-year absence.

Below the podium positions, though, there was some news. The BYD Yuan Up and Leapmotor A10 are surfing the B-segment wave and both climbed a position, to 5th and 6th, respectively.

If the BYD Yuan Up continues on its current record streak, then the small crossover could even aim to surpass the #4 FCB Ti7 before the year ends.

Still, with three subcompacts presently in the top 6 (Geely Xingyuan, BYD Yuan Up, and Leapmotor A10), small is hot right now, in China.

Elsewhere, the BYD Sealion 05 was up two positions, to 16th, while the Wuling Mini EV is hoping to bring tiny city cars back into the spotlight, and in October, it jumped two positions, ending the month in 13th….

Looking at the overall manufacturer ranking, it is a sea of red. Everyone is losing sales — substantial time. The exception is #5 Leapmotor (+31% YoY), while #8 Xiaomi (+3% YoY) and #10 Xpeng (+0%) are just hanging on.

So, now, not only are foreign OEMs suffering (Nissan was down 70% in October, Honda was down 51%), but even domestic ones are being affected by the EV shift.

Some may be asking, “But what about #9 Nevo and its 125% growth rate?” Well, it isn’t so much that they are winning sales, but they are effectively replacing the sales of their mother brand, Changan, which in October was only 19th after a 60% drop in sales YoY.

Looking at the auto brand ranking, BYD is firmly in the leadership position (17.2%), while runner-up Geely held to its 7.1% market share.

Industry observers note that rising 3rd placed Leapmotor (6.7%, up 0.2%) is fast approaching Geely. It wouldn’t be surprising if the startup brand became the upcoming silver medalist in the final days of the year.

One thing is for certain though — Leapmotor will win its first medal this year. The only question is the material that it will be made of….

Recent findings suggest that speaking of position changes, Tesla had a horrible month (4.4%, down from 4.9% in September), which allowed Wuling (4.6%) to climb one position in October, into 4th. At the end of the year, expect Tesla to keep the #4 position, as its December peak should help it surpass Wuling.

Looking at OEMs/automotive groups/alliances, BYD is leading with 21.9% share of the market, up 0.1% in October.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Geely remained in second with 11.8% share. The multinational conglomerate has the runner-up spot secured.

According to recent reports, #3 SAIC was stable (8%) and remained firm in the last place on the podium, while #4 Leapmotor (6.7%, up 0.2%) remained on the rise. Will we see the startup challenge SAIC in 2027 for the 3rd spot?

Latest Update: Walking and weight training may not be enough to keep your bones strong

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the type of exercise you do may be more important for your bones than how long you spend doing it.
  • The findings, published in Sports Medicine - Open, suggest that certain fast-paced sports may provide greater benefits for bone metabolism than walking or conventional strength training.
  • To investigate how different forms of exercise affect bones, the Semmelweis University team reviewed 24 clinical studies involving 1,238 healthy adults.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the type of exercise you do may be more important for your bones than how long you spend doing it. Researchers at Semmelweis University have found that intense physical activity involving sudden bursts of movement, quick changes in direction, and sharp turns appears especially effective at stimulating fresh bone formation.

The findings, published in Sports Medicine - Open, suggest that certain fast-paced sports may provide greater benefits for bone metabolism than walking or conventional strength training. The research could help scientists develop more effective exercise recommendations for preserving bone health and reducing the risk of osteoporosis.

Why Exercise Intensity Matters for Bone Health.

To investigate how different forms of exercise affect bones, the Semmelweis University team reviewed 24 clinical studies involving 1,238 healthy adults.

Instead of relying on bone mineral density measurements, which can take considerable time to reveal changes, the researchers examined blood markers associated with the production of latest bone tissue. These biological indicators can reveal how bones respond to exercise within a matter of weeks, allowing scientists to detect changes much sooner.

"What makes our study unique is that we examined not only the type of exercise - whether endurance, resistance, or combined training - but also exercise intensity, frequency, and duration. Our goal was to determine which forms of exercise stimulate bone metabolism most effectively and which appear to be less beneficial from this perspective," noted Dr. Péter Ferdinandy, Vice-Rector for Science and Innovations at Semmelweis University and senior author of the study.

Football and Handball Show Surprising Bone Benefits.

The strongest responses were associated with vigorous sports that repeatedly require players to accelerate, change direction, turn, and make powerful movements.

Recent findings suggest that recreational football and handball stood out in particular. These activities were linked to increases of up to 45-46 percent in blood markers associated with bone formation, suggesting that they may provide a particularly strong stimulus for the body's bone-building processes.

It has been revealed that more conventional activities generally produced smaller responses. Walking, step aerobics, and standard resistance workouts performed in the gym were less effective at stimulating the measured indicators of bone formation.

The findings were especially unexpected for resistance training, which is commonly recommended as a way to support skeletal health.

"The most surprising finding was that resistance training did not produce a significant effect on markers of bone metabolism, even though several professional guidelines recommend this type of exercise for maintaining bone health. Likewise, low- or moderate-intensity endurance exercise, such as walking or jogging, highlighted no meaningful long-term effect," explained Viktória Barna, PhD student at Semmelweis University and first author of the study.

Why Walking and Weight Training Still Matter.

The results do not suggest that walking, jogging, or other less demanding activities should be abandoned. These forms of exercise continue to offer vital health benefits, even if they do not stimulate the measured bone-building processes as strongly as more intense sports.

Rather, the research indicates that maintaining healthy bones may require greater mechanical stimulation than many everyday activities provide. Movements that place more substantial forces on the skeleton appear to produce a stronger response in the biological processes involved in forming new bone.

However, the researchers stress that people should not suddenly begin strenuous exercise without preparing appropriately.

In a recent development, this is especially vital for individuals with cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, or metabolic conditions, as well as those who already have osteoporosis. Anyone in these groups who is considering a latest activity or a more physically demanding exercise routine should first speak with their treating physician, general practitioner, or a sports medicine specialist. Medical guidance can help determine whether the activity and its intensity are suitable for their health and physical capabilities.

Could High-Intensity Exercise Help Prevent Osteoporosis?

Sources indicate that the findings offer a upcoming perspective on how exercise could be used to maintain bone health as people age. While the analysis focused on markers of bone metabolism rather than direct changes in bone density, the results suggest that vigorous activity may encourage early biological changes that support bone formation.

"According to the World Health Organization, regular physical activity offers numerous health benefits. However, our findings suggest that low-intensity exercise alone is not sufficient to stimulate bone metabolism. High-intensity exercise may trigger early beneficial changes in bone formation, potentially helping to slow bone loss and support healthy aging," summarized Dr. Nóra Sydó, clinical specialist and co-author of the study.

The researchers believe that understanding which movements most effectively stimulate bone formation could lead to better exercise programs designed to preserve skeletal strength and help prevent osteoporosis.

For now, the findings highlight an notable distinction: staying physically active is beneficial for overall health, but keeping bones healthy over the long term may depend not only on how much people move, but also on how powerfully and dynamically they move.

Materials provided by Semmelweis University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#76495. These 7 Porsches Have A Reputation For Being Nearly Indestructible

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1998 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

These 7 Porsches Have A Reputation For Being Nearly Indestructible

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for many, owning a Porsche is something of a dream.
  • It's models like the 996-generation 911 that might give buyers a reason to pause, as while the right advice could save 996 buyers from getting screwed, the model is still plagued with complex issues.
  • Recent findings suggest that that need not end the dream for Porsche fans, though, as there is still a plethora of used Porsches that have proven pretty much indestructible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for many, owning a Porsche is something of a dream. However, keeping one running as it should year after year without having to spend thousands in preventative maintenance or labor-intensive repairs might not be all that easy. Sure, the automaker enjoys a reputation for engineering excellence, but that doesn't mean each model from its back catalog is as capable as the last when it comes to covering moon mileage.

It's models like the 996-generation 911 that might give buyers a reason to pause, as while the right advice could save 996 buyers from getting screwed, the model is still plagued with complex issues. Problems such as failed intermediate shaft (IMS) bearings and cylinder bore scoring promptly make the 996 look less of a tempting proposition for those who need something they can rely upon.

Recent findings suggest that that need not end the dream for Porsche fans, though, as there is still a plethora of used Porsches that have proven pretty much indestructible. Some are cheap, like the 987.2-generation Boxster, and some are far from it, such as the iconic "widowmaker" 930 Turbo. What they all prove, however, is that with the correct maintenance and know-how, a secondhand Porsche really can run forever. Here are seven of our favorites, listed from the oldest through to the newest, and justified via high-mileage examples, owner reviews, and expert opinions.

It can be difficult to deduce whether the Porsche 924 was a success. It sold rather well, with a total of 152,082 finding homes across its full production window, 1976 to 1988. However, it sat unloved for decades, with many enthusiasts citing its lackluster performance and what they erroneously called its van-derived engine as solid proof that it wasn't a "proper" Porsche.

In a recent development, the eventual 924 Turbo and homologation special 924 Carrera GT models did much to align the little coupé with enthusiasts, but for our purposes here, it's the naturally aspirated 2.0-liter inline-4-powered model that appeals the most. The Classics World 924 Buyer's Guide describes it as remarkably robust, and says "simple DIY maintenance" is often all that's required to keep it running. The guide adds that 924 spare parts are available directly through the automaker via Porsche's Classic program, and are frequently quite affordable.

Sources indicate that numerous enthusiasts on owners forums are happy to boast that their own pride-and-joys have been able to surpass 100,000 miles, and often by some serious margins. One post on Porsche Club Great Britain details both a 168,000-mile and 272,000-mile example, and that post is almost 20 years old, so many more examples may well have hit such achievements since. Owner reviews further back up the 924's claim to indestructibility, saying that, in spite of its age, the little Porsche largely proves very dependable across long ownership windows.

While the Porsche 924 is impressively reliable and durable, it probably isn't the adrenaline-fueled sports car that springs into most minds when the word "Porsche" is uttered. Instead, something like the original 930 Turbo is far more appropriate.

It has been revealed that it was produced between the 1975 and '89 model years, and throughout that time the engine evolved from a turbocharged 3.0-liter flat-6 with 256 horsepower into a boosted 3.3-liter unit that produced 296 horses. U.S. versions received slightly less power, but these were still very formidable sports cars for the era.

Industry observers note that turbochargers do add extra complexity into engines, and they can fail prematurely, so it might be reasonable to assume the 930 Turbo doesn't fall into the "indestructible" category. Well, you'd be wrong to assume that, and one man alone proves that point impeccably. His name is Bill MacEachern, and he ordered a 930 Turbo back when they were fresh in '76. He's kept it ever since, and racked up in excess of 826,000 miles during that time. Yes, its engine has been rebuilt, but he's had it tuned to produce in excess of 550 horsepower, and it's still managing its daily duties without stress. Here he is on Magnacars telling the story:.

Those seeking to find themselves an indestructible 930 Turbo for piling on the miles should head for a 3.3-liter model. These received internal improvements over the earlier cars, like different sealing rings that could deal with heat more effectively, enabling the engine to handle its performance more reliably. Also, the addition of an intercooler massively reduced intake temperatures on 3.3-powered cars, as well as helping to bring that extra grunt.

According to recent reports, if a boosted Porsche 911 from the late '70s is capable of punching out 800,000-plus miles, it stands to reason that a less performance-focused 911 of the same era also makes for a pretty dependable companion. The SC introduced fresh technologies and developments in the engine bay that really helped boost reliability.

The previous model was powered by a 2.7-liter mill, the last evolution of the 911's original engine. By this point, it was at its limit, and with thermal reactors used to help reduce emissions in line with upcoming legislation, heat was a major issue. This heat buildup caused head stud and valve complications, and while fixable via the aftermarket route, such issues plagued the reliability reputation of early '70s 911s. The later SC rectified this issue with an all-aluminum engine casing that could better handle the engine's higher temperatures, and those thermal reactors were replaced with catalytic converters, which ran far cooler.

Industry observers note that it's well-documented that these 3.0-liter SC models are good for 200,000 miles or more between engine rebuilds, as long as they are suitably maintained. So if it's an early 911 with built-in indestructibility that you're seeking, this is a far better starting point than any pre-'77 car. In fact, Porsche Club GB describes the 3.0-liter as "probably the most reliable Porsche engine ever" and "simple to work on." Just be prepared for the prices commanded; we recently found a 164,000-mile 911 SC selling for close to $75,000, so even with high mileage, these cars are still a significant investment.

This next entry steers us back away from Porsche's legendary line of rear-engined flat-6-powered models, and once again to a four-cylinder front-engined sports coupé. The Porsche 944, much like the 924, was available in a variety of guises, but for reliability and durability, the simple naturally aspirated models appeal the most.

Industry observers note that its 2.5-liter engine (displacement grew throughout production) is derived from the V8-powered 928, and it's known to have a remarkably strong bottom end. While the Turbo cars aren't exactly fragile, these later boosted engines are more complex, and failures can and do occur, as both turbo exhaust manifolds and wastegates can crack. In terms of what a base 944 can achieve, it's well-documented that these engines are good for in excess of 250,000 miles before a rebuild is necessary, provided necessary maintenance is kept up with along the way.

According to recent reports, looking at owner reviews, the 944 experience seems to be mostly trouble-free. Across 127 reviews on CarSurvey, the 944 received a 7.5 out of 10 score for reliability. One owner of a high-mileage example noted that, while certain items like locks, alarms, and other accessories were beginning to fail, they were easily DIY-able, and no power train concerns were noted, despite the car having north of 160,000 miles.

Sources indicate that some owners would say a 160,000-mile 944 is still just being broken in. In 2023 a 571,000-mile example was spotted at an auto auction, and even boosted models have been seen with 400,000 miles on the clock, who knows how far a well-maintained 944 can go?

The 3.2-powered Carrera models follow on from the SC, which is a textbook example of an indestructible Porsche. The Carrera 3.2 is less bulletproof than the earlier 3.0 SC, with some experts suggesting it may need top-end work by 130,000 miles, whereas SC cars can exceed that mileage and more without having to come apart. That doesn't mean, however, that the Carrera 3.2 isn't worthy of a place here.

It has been revealed that in fact, the 3.2-liter engine received a plethora of updates that 3.0-liter engines miss out on. Upcoming pistons, hydraulic timing chain tensioners, and a new Bosch Motronic engine management system were chief among the updates, bringing more power, efficiency, and reliability, especially in the timing system.

Regardless of whether the Carrera 3.2 is as bulletproof as its 3.0-liter SC predecessor, it's a fine place to look for a durable classic Porsche. While some do argue the top end may need work by 130,000 miles, others say 200,000 miles is perfectly possible before a rebuild is required. A very smart 218,000-mile example sold this year at auction in the U.K., described by Historics Auctioneers as "One of the best maintained G Series cars we have offered." Admittedly, it had been treated to an engine rebuild and glass-out repaint in recent years, so both its engine and body should be good for another 200,000 miles or so.

The last two entries on our list bring things back up to date, at least a little. While the latest batch of Porsches very well could be the holy grail of reliability and indestructibility, they simply haven't been on the road long enough to prove it, which is why most models here are far older. They've had the chance to accumulate hundreds of thousands of miles and demonstrate their strength.

Recent findings suggest that one such model is the first-generation Porsche Cayenne, specifically the 3.2-liter model. It's powered by Volkswagen's 30-year-old VR6 engine, which was already well-known by the time Porsche's 955-generation Cayenne debuted as a 2004 model. Why the 3.2? Well, it boasts a strong cast-iron block, whereas the V8 models sported aluminum blocks, and serious engine concerns are quite uncommon.

According to recent reports, the 3.2-liter VR6 engine is certainly capable of completing 200,000 miles with basic maintenance covered, and what's just as reassuring, is that the rest of the Cayenne seems built just as tough. One owner on Pistonheads thoroughly detailed every expense during their 51,000-mile and five-year ownership of a Cayenne 3.2 that was already 100,000 miles and 10 years into life when purchased. Apart from general servicing, some tidying up, and a few minor repairs, the Cayenne wanted for nothing, and was sold on to continue its service. Porsche's brand-newly introduced Cayenne Turbo Electric might be an impressive $200,000 powerhouse of excellence, but if robust dependability is called for, perhaps its nameplate forefather is the better bet.

Recent findings suggest that we called the 2024 Porsche 718 Boxster GTS 4.0 perfection on wheels, and while it's not a model that's attracting much negative attention to itself, it's barely old enough to call reliable yet, let alone indestructible. The 987.2-generation of Boxster and Cayman, though, is another matter altogether, especially in base 2.9-liter flat-6 guise. While the 3.4-liter "S" model is a better performer, it has been known to suffer bore-scoring, while the 2.9-liter lump seems to avoid that costly concern. Porsche specialist LN Engineering claims it has "never seen a case of cylinder bore scoring with these models," when referring to the 987.2 Cayman and Boxster.

Industry observers note that it's also important to detail why it's the 987.2 cars which deserve a spot here, rather than the 987.1 models. The later models employed an all-newly introduced 9A1 engine, which did away with the troublesome IMS bearing altogether. All previous iterations of the Boxster and Cayman were motivated by M96 and M97 engines, which did suffer from IMS problems.

It would appear most owners find the rest of the car to be just as dependable. Across 12 reviews on Cars, specifically for 2010 model-year Boxsters, owners rated the drop-top a respectable 4.4 out of 5 on reliability. Most comments commended the car's sublime road manners, but some did point out their Boxster had been nothing but reliable, which should reassure potential future owners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the digital world has revolutionized how real estate is marketed and sold, placing a premium on strategic online presence and data-driven advertising. Among the myriad online tools available, Schema Markup stands out as an extremely potent weapon for real estate agents. This article offers a comprehensive look at how real estate agents can effectively use Schema Markup to bolster their online presence, increase organic reach, and drive sales.

In a recent development, before discussing its application, let's first demystify what Schema Markup is. Schema Markup, also known as Structured Data, is a form of microdata. Once added to a webpage, it creates an enhanced description (commonly known as a rich snippet), which appears in search results. Developed by a collaborative team from Google, Yahoo!, Bing, and Yandex, Schema.org was launched in 2011 to create and support a common set of schemas for structured data markup on web pages.

Industry observers note that to break it down simply, Schema Markup tells the search engine what your data means, not just what it claims. This enhanced understanding allows search engines to present more detailed and accurate snippets of your site to consumers, increasing click-through rates (CTR), boosting organic search rankings, and potentially improving conversion rates.

Why Real Estate Agents Need Schema Markup.

In a recent development, schema Markup is incredibly beneficial to real estate professionals. The real estate industry is hyper-local, and search engine queries reflect this. Buyers and sellers are often searching with a specific location in mind. A real estate agent using Schema Markup can provide rich, location-based information directly in search results, making their listings more likely to be clicked on. It's an opportunity to outshine competitors and improve visibility in local search results.

In a recent development, furthermore, Schema Markup helps real estate websites become more comprehensible to search engines. This enhanced understanding translates into more accurate categorization, increased visibility, and a better chance of appearing in relevant search results. In a landscape where digital prominence equates to business success, Schema Markup is no longer a luxury but a necessity for every real estate agent.

Implementing Schema Markup for Real Estate.

Now that we understand why Schema Markup is crucial, let's look at how real estate agents can effectively implement it.

It can significantly enhance your search engine visibility, increase click-through rates, and ultimately contribute to driving more leads and sales. With patience and precision, implementing Schema Markup can provide an appreciable uptick in your digital marketing efforts and become an integral part of your online strategy.

#76489. Industry News: 7 Luxury Cars Most Likely To Last 200,000 Miles

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2084 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Jalopnik ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: 7 Luxury Cars Most Likely To Last 200,000 Miles

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2084 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, buying a new car is more expensive than ever, and if you want something from an established luxury or premium brand, it's going to cost you even more.
  • However, just because you spend massive bucks on a luxury vehicle doesn't mean it will be reliable.
  • According to recent reports, we examined reliability ratings, longevity studies, and ownership data from various sources, including an iSeeCars study on the longest-lasting models.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, buying a new car is more expensive than ever, and if you want something from an established luxury or premium brand, it's going to cost you even more. Of course, when you're spending more, you expect to get more in return. On top of the prestige that comes with driving a luxury brand, you're probably expecting nicer materials, more equipment, and a better dealership experience when compared to mainstream brands. And another thing you want for your money is a vehicle that lasts. If you are spending significant bucks for an Audi or Mercedes-Benz, you should expect it to last for 200,000 miles without needing three transmissions, two engine rebuilds, and a daily prayer.

However, just because you spend massive bucks on a luxury vehicle doesn't mean it will be reliable. Just ask anyone who's owned a Land Rover after the original warranty expired. On the other hand, you don't need to resign yourself to driving a Toyota Corolla if you want to see 200,000 miles displayed on your odometer. The trick is knowing which luxury vehicles you should take a chance on, and that's what this list is all about.

According to recent reports, we examined reliability ratings, longevity studies, and ownership data from various sources, including an iSeeCars study on the longest-lasting models. You'll see SUVs, wagons, and sedans on this list, although you'll also only see a few cars from the same manufacturer. Otherwise, this would pretty much just be a list of current Lexus models. Lexus does make some very reliable vehicles, but its cars are not the only options if you want something that lasts.

It has been revealed that the Acura MDX has a 13.1% chance of reaching 250,000 miles. Although that's a relatively low percentage, it's 2.4 times better than the average vehicle and 50,000 miles above what this list is looking for. In other words, reaching the 200,000-mile mark is a very achievable feat for this model. The three-row luxury SUV starts at $53,350, which includes the destination and handling fee. It might not get front row parking at the finest restaurant in town, but the MDX can be loaded up with luxury touches if you opt for certain packages. Those touches include open-pore wood accents, contrast stitching on the Milano leather interior, and a premium Bang & Olufsen Sound System, as well as a panoramic moonroof which comes standard on all models.

It has been revealed that the front-wheel-drive MDX is powered by a 3.5-liter V6 producing 290 horsepower and 267 pound-feet of torque. That's also the case for its all-wheel-drive A-Spec trim, which can be kitted out with even more niceties like a surround-view camera and 20-inch wheels. The highest-end model you can get is the Type S Advance, which gets a twin-scroll turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 good for 355 horses and 354 pound-feet. A Type S with just about every option tops out around $80,000. None of these features are particularly cutting-edge, but that's exactly why this SUV is so reliable. Another feather in the cap of the MDX is that it's safe, too, with the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) naming it a Top Safety Pick. It isn't the flashiest luxury vehicle out there, but it will do everything it needs to do for as long as you need it to.

It might be surprising to see an Audi on this list. After all, German cars don't typically hold the same reliability reputation as the Japanese automakers, with Consumer Reports giving fresh Audi vehicles a middling ranking when it comes to predicted reliability. However, some models from the brand fare better than others. The Audi S3 ranked as the most reliable luxury subcompact car under $60,000, per iSeeCars. To be fair, only two cars were in that category, but it also ranked eighth among 35 luxury small cars for reliability. Most of the cars ranked above it are either out of production or Lexus models that aren't being included on this list to keep it from being too Lexus-centric.

Kelley Blue Book (KBB) rated the 2025 Audi S3 as number one in the Best Luxury Compact Cars category based on performance, reliability, safety and other factors. The organization also gave the Audi S3 an above-average reliability rating, while S3 owners on the website gave it a perfect five out of five score. All in all, it isn't unreasonable to expect this model to reach 200,000 miles.

Industry observers note that powering the $53,895 Audi S3 is the fourth-generation EA888 engine. The turbocharged DOHC 16-valve inline-four makes 328 horsepower and 295 pound-feet of torque. It will rocket to 60 mph in just over four seconds, but it has a lot more going for it than straight-line speed. Inside is a 15-speaker Sonos sound system and the Audi Virtual Cockpit plus. Optionally, you can add Nappa leather seats for $1,000 and a Driver Assistance package that includes surround view cameras and adaptive cruise control for $1,800.

No automaker is perfect, but it's hard to argue against how dominant Toyota and Lexus are when it comes to reliability. In the aforementioned iSeeCars study on vehicle reliability, nine of the top 10 vehicles are either Toyota or Lexus models. The Lexus GX in particular has a 23.3% chance of reaching 250,000 miles, which is 4.3 times higher than average. The redesigned GX 550 arrived for the 2024 model year with a twin-turbocharged 3.4-liter V6 and substantially more modern technology. You could argue that the new generation GX has not been out long enough to determine true long-term reliability, but the reputation of Lexus has earned this model some leeway to make it onto this list.

Recent findings suggest that the GX is a traditional body-on-frame SUV that offers genuine off-road ability and the strength to endure many years of trail bashing. All GX trims, including the entry-level $69,085 GX 550 Premium, get the same engine making 349 horsepower and 479 pound-feet of torque. With the over-$76,000 Overtrail trim, the GX can tow up to 9,096 pounds, which is within 150 pounds of a Ford F-150 SuperCrew 4x4 with the 5.0-liter V8 engine. Alternatively, the over-$81,000 Luxury trim will get you heated and ventilated semi-aniline leather seats that have massage functionality, as well as a 21-speaker Mark Levinson sound system.

The Lexus IS is an interesting car because it has plenty of luxury features to justify the Lexus badge and price point — and yet, it is surprisingly old-school. There are no turbochargers or hybrid systems to add complexity. Under the hood is a naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 from the legendary Toyota 2GR engine series. In other words, getting a couple hundred thousand miles out of this engine should be no sweat. And the iSeeCars study agrees, as the IS has a 17.5% chance to reach 250,000 miles – 3.3 times higher than average.

Starting at $47,545, the IS is the least-expensive Lexus sedan in the current lineup. But that doesn't stop it from including all the luxury touches you would expect from the brand. That includes the standard Forged Bamboo center console, the 12.3-inch touchscreen, and a matching digital instrument cluster. Extra luxuries like the 17-speaker Mark Levinson audio system can be found in the Special Appearance Package, which will run you a little over $60,000. It's a good pick if you're looking for something fancy that will also let you circumnavigate the Earth eight times over.

It has been revealed that historically, if you wanted a luxury car to last at least 200,000 miles, you'd just buy a Lexus LS. It might not be the fanciest car in the world, but it's practically as reliable than the sunrise — and it's probably the most likely car on this list to make it to that mileage target. It has a 38.8% chance of reaching 250,000 miles, putting it 7.2 times higher than the average car. On top of that, iSeeCars measured the Lexus LS 500 as having an average lifespan of 226,558 miles. Yes, even the average LS 500 is likely to break the 200,000-mile barrier. Go back in history and you will find some that go much further, like Matt Farah's LS 400, which managed to cross the million-mile threshold.

Sources indicate that though, the biggest hurdle to getting a Lexus LS 500 to last for 200,000 miles might be actually buying one. The LS lineup is going out of production after nearly 40 years, and to mark the occasion, Lexus is building just 250 Heritage Edition LS 500s. At $99,280, you won't get much change back from your $100,000 bill. But you will get a panoramic glass roof, a Laser Special Black premium wood trim, a 23-speaker Mark Levinson Surround Sound system, and more. Plus, like all LS 500s, you'll get a twin-turbocharged 3.4-liter V6 that makes 416 horsepower and 442 pound-feet of torque. It's a shame to see the LS go, but given its history of reliability, you'll likely still see it on the road for decades to come.

Industry observers note that while every Mercedes-Benz may not be a paragon of reliability, there are some models that stand above the rest. We put the Mercedes-Benz E-Class Wagon on this list not just because it is reliable, but also because it's one of the best station wagons of all time. Wagons only make up about 1% of upcoming vehicle sales in the U.S., yet the people who buy them tend to love them and want to keep them for a while. For those folks, the Mercedes-Benz E-Class Wagon is an excellent choice.

It has been revealed that the E-Class wagon has a 7.5% chance to hit 250,000 miles, which is 2.2 times higher than average. Additionally, the iSeeCars recall study lists the E-Class as one of the least likely vehicles to be recalled over a 30-year lifespan, with an expected recall rate of just 0.2 in those three decades. For the sake of comparison, the Lincoln Aviator has a recall rate of 94.2 recalls during that same time span. Not having a vehicle recalled doesn't mean it will last for 200,000 miles, but it does reflect the model's attention to detail and build quality.

For the E-Class's most luxurious offerings, a new 2027 E 450 4MATIC All-Terrain starts at $81,450. It comes with standard features such as dual-zone climate control, a panorama roof, and a power liftgate. You can also add ventilated and massaging front seats, Nappa leather upholstery, and more features if your budget can handle it (with an increase of $2,600 for the top-of-the-line Pinnacle trim). It's all powered by an engine making 375 horsepower and 369 pound-feet of torque. If you have an extra $15,000 to spare, there's also a hybrid model available with even more luxury features, and its horsepower and torque figures increase to 577 and 553, respectively.

Today, you can get an SUV from just about every automaker, from Aston Martin to Rolls-Royce. But the Mercedes-Benz G-Class is still one of the most luxurious off-road SUVs you can buy, and unlike some others, it can also handle some very challenging terrain. The G-Class has a 17.3% estimated chance of reaching 250,000 miles, which is more than three times the average. The Mercedes-Benz G-Class also has an average lifespan of 187,916 miles, so 200,000 is not much of a stretch. iSeeCars ranked it number one out of 18 vehicles in the Most Reliable Luxury Large SUVs category. Plus, the G-Class has the same minuscule expected recall rate as the E-Class.

None of this comes cheap, though. The least expensive G-Class, with 443 horsepower and 413 pound-feet of torque, starts at over $153,000. Sure, buying a substantial, heavy vehicle like this can save you thousands on your taxes. And that substantial starting price includes luxuries such as leather upholstery, heated front seats and armrests, three-zone climate control, and heated and cooled cup holders. But the G-Class will also be on the expensive side to operate. You need to fill it with premium gas, and fuel economy runs in the teens. You'll also be paying Mercedes-Benz prices for maintenance and service.

Still, if you stay on top of it, the G-Class should last a very long time — and that goes for any vehicle on this list. If you want them to last 200,000 or even 300,000 miles, following the maintenance schedule is just one tip that you should follow. Doing that will help these already reliable vehicles last for even longer.
